verdictRationale: The spec is directionally solid, but it still has enforceability gaps around registry authority, install atomicity, and status semantics. These are fixable, but they affect whether the registry can actually be trusted as the source of truth under failure or migration conditions.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A capability appears as installed in generated registry or inventory even though its visible files, adapter outputs, or doctor checks failed during install.
falsifiability.observableSignal: After a failed or partially failed install, INVENTORY.md or registries/capabilities.yml advertises a capability that cannot be invoked or is absent from the visible capability folders.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Run an install fixture with one valid capability and one capability whose MCP smoke check fails after registry generation; inspect capabilities.yml, INVENTORY.md, lockfile, and generated adapters to verify whether failed capability state is accurately represented and whether stale generated files remain.
falsifiability.threshold: No failed capability may be marked status: installed; failed installs must either roll back generated artifacts or persist a typed broken/failed state with matching lockfile doctor evidence.

newIssueList.title: Installed status is not coherently defined
newIssueList.description: The Vision says a capability is installed only when it has registry records, visible files or links, generated adapters, and passing doctor checks recorded in the lockfile. But the deterministic generation flow writes registries and capabilities.yml before doctor runs, and the capability record includes status values such as installed and broken without defining when transitions occur. Under failure, the system can advertise installed capabilities before the evidence required by the definition exists.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a lifecycle state machine: declared -> materialized -> adapter_generated -> doctor_passed -> installed, with failed transitions producing broken or install_failed records. State whether failed installs roll back generated artifacts or persist partial state explicitly.
newIssueList.lineRef: Vision; Capability Record Contract; Deterministic Generation steps 3-8

newIssueList.title: Registry source of truth conflicts with generated normalized registry
newIssueList.description: The spec says specialized registries are source-controlled or generated from package declarations, then normalized into capabilities.yml. The Risks section says capabilities.yml should be generated or digest-checked if edited independently, but this remains undecided. If both specialized registries and capabilities.yml can be edited or generated, there is no single authoritative write path to enforce drift prevention.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Make `registries/capabilities.yml` explicitly generated and non-authoritative in v0, or explicitly source-controlled with mandatory digest reconciliation. Add acceptance criteria that manual edits to generated normalized output are rejected or overwritten deterministically.

newIssueList.title: Adapter gate cannot validate all adapter-introduced behavior
newIssueList.description: The adapter gate compares emitted adapter items against capability ids and types, but adapters such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md may introduce behavior through prose rules, command snippets, or referenced files that do not map cleanly to a typed item set. The spec does not define how candidate adapter sets are extracted from Markdown adapters or what counts as a command, hook, rule, or skill reference. This makes the strongest alignment guarantee only partially enforceable.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define adapter manifests as structured intermediate outputs for each generated adapter, and require the gate to validate those manifests before rendering Markdown/TOML. For Markdown adapters, generated prose must come from registered rule records and include traceable source ids.
newIssueList.lineRef: Deterministic Generation; Acceptance Criteria; Adapter gate validation

newIssueList.title: Local override semantics are underspecified
newIssueList.description: The spec allows `agentic-os.local.json` overrides for local paths and disabled capabilities, and includes local overrides in lockfile digest inputs. It does not define whether local overrides can change visibility, customer_safe, harness targets, launch commands, env requirements, or doctor behavior. Without this boundary, local config could silently bypass package intent or customer safety enforcement.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define an allowlist of local override fields for v0, such as local path substitutions and disabled capability ids only. Explicitly forbid overriding safety classification, visibility, provides/requires, hook side effects, and adapter target identity.

newIssueList.title: Fresh install and migration enforcement are conflated
newIssueList.description: Acceptance criteria require strict install failures for missing registries and adapter-introduced items, while P3 says migration tooling will propose records and report gaps before enforcing strict install failure on legacy installs. The spec does not separate fresh installs, managed upgrades, and legacy migrations as different modes with different failure behavior. That ambiguity can make migration either destructive or too permissive.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add explicit install modes: `fresh`, `upgrade-managed`, and `migrate-legacy`, with mode-specific enforcement thresholds and mutation rules. Legacy migration should produce proposals without writing adapters unless explicitly accepted.

newIssueList.title: Schema ownership and validation format are missing
newIssueList.description: The spec requires YAML schemas for every registry type but does not specify where schemas live, what schema language is used, or how package authors validate records before install. Without schema location and invocation rules, the validation contract is not reproducible by contributors or automation.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Add a `schemas/registries/` layout and name the schema format, for example JSON Schema over parsed YAML. Require `agentic-os validate` to run schema, normalization, adapter gate, inventory, doctor, and secret hygiene checks as separate reportable phases.

preserveList.summary: The spec correctly makes harness dot folders generated adapters rather than authoritative sources of capability identity.
The explicit registry table and normalized capability record give the implementation a concrete target instead of leaving discovery as prose.
The customer-safety and secret-hygiene requirements are valuable and should remain first-class validation checks.
preserveList.lineRef: Capability Record Contract; Acceptance Criteria; Validations
